faqs.answer: Philippicus revived the Monothelite heresy condemned in 681. Rome refused to display his image or use his name in official acts until an orthodox emperor, Anastasius II, replaced him.

directAnswer: Pope St. Gregory II, a Roman, reigned from 715 to 731. He sent St. Boniface to evangelize Germany, encouraged the refounding of Monte Cassino, resisted the iconoclast policies and taxes of Emperor Leo III, and received from the Lombard king Liutprand the town of Sutri, often seen as the first step toward the Papal States.

sections.h2: Librarian, Deacon, and Companion to Constantinople
paras: Gregory was born in Rome, the son of Marcellus, and was raised in the papal household from a young age. Under Sergius I he became a subdeacon, treasurer, and later librarian of the Roman Church. As a deacon he accompanied Pope Constantine to Constantinople in 710–711, where his learning impressed Justinian II during the discussions about the Quinisext canons. He was elected pope in 715.

Early in his reign he began repairing the walls of Rome, a work interrupted by a severe flood of the Tiber. He also restored churches and founded or renewed monasteries and hospices for the poor and the elderly.

sections.h2: Boniface and the Rebuilding of Monte Cassino
paras: In 719 Gregory received the English monk Wynfrith in Rome, gave him the name Boniface, and commissioned him to preach to the pagan peoples east of the Rhine. In 722 he consecrated him a bishop, bound him by oath to the Roman see, and gave him letters of recommendation to Charles Martel. Boniface became the great apostle of Germany. Gregory also sent envoys to organize the church in Bavaria at the request of Duke Theodo.

Monte Cassino, the monastery of St. Benedict, had lain in ruins since the Lombards destroyed it in the late sixth century. Around 717, with Gregory's encouragement, the monk Petronax of Brescia led its refoundation, and it became once again a major center of Benedictine life. In 721 Gregory held a synod in Rome that issued canons on marriage, forbidding unions within close degrees of kinship and with consecrated women.

sections.h2: Leo III, Iconoclasm, and the Donation of Sutri
paras: In the 720s Emperor Leo III imposed heavy new taxes on Italy, which Gregory resisted, and imperial officials reportedly plotted against his life. When Leo moved against the veneration of icons around 726–730, Gregory opposed the policy firmly. Letters attributed to him defending icons survive, but their authenticity is debated. Even so, he discouraged Italian rebels from setting up a rival emperor, seeking to defend the faith without breaking with the empire.

The Lombard king Liutprand, meanwhile, was expanding his territory. In 728 he seized the fortress of Sutri north of Rome but, at Gregory's urging, gave it back as a gift to the apostles Peter and Paul. Historians often regard this Donation of Sutri as the first territorial grant that would grow into the Papal States. Gregory died on 11 February 731, his feast day.

keyFacts: Reign: 19 May 715 – 11 February 731
Born in Rome; former librarian of the Roman Church
Commissioned St. Boniface (719) and consecrated him bishop (722)
Held the Synod of Rome (721) on marriage law
Received the Donation of Sutri from King Liutprand (728); feast day February 11

faqs.question: How was Pope Gregory II connected to St. Boniface?
faqs.answer: Gregory gave the English monk Wynfrith the name Boniface in 719, sent him to evangelize the Germanic peoples, and consecrated him a bishop in 722.

faqs.question: What was the Donation of Sutri?
faqs.answer: In 728 the Lombard king Liutprand returned the captured town of Sutri to the papacy as a gift to the apostles Peter and Paul. It is often considered the first step in the formation of the Papal States.

faqs.question: How did Gregory II respond to iconoclasm?
faqs.answer: He opposed Emperor Leo III's measures against the veneration of icons, while still urging Italians not to revolt against the empire or set up a rival emperor.

directAnswer: Pope St. Gregory III, a Syrian, reigned from 731 to 741. He condemned iconoclasm at Roman synods, strengthened St. Boniface's mission by naming him an archbishop, and appealed to Charles Martel for help against the Lombards. He was the last pope born outside Europe until Francis in 2013.

sections.h2: Elected by Acclamation at a Funeral
paras: Gregory was born in Syria, the son of a man named John, and was a priest in Rome known for his learning in Greek and Latin and his knowledge of the Psalms. The Roman people acclaimed him as pope during the funeral of Gregory II in February 731. He was consecrated in March after receiving the approval of the exarch in Ravenna; he is generally regarded as the last pope to seek such approval from an imperial representative.

sections.h2: Synods Against Iconoclasm
paras: Gregory first sent letters to Emperor Leo III protesting his policy against holy images, but his envoy was detained. In November 731 he held a synod in Rome, attended by many Italian bishops, which decreed excommunication for anyone who removed, destroyed, or profaned images of Christ, the Virgin Mary, the apostles, and the saints.

Leo III retaliated, and at some point confiscated the papal estates in Sicily and southern Italy and is said to have transferred the dioceses of southern Italy and Illyricum from Roman to Constantinopolitan jurisdiction. Historians debate whether these measures came under Gregory III or later. Gregory, for his part, encouraged the veneration of images in Rome, adding icons and decorations to St. Peter's and other churches, including an oratory in St. Peter's honoring the Savior, his Mother, and all the saints.

sections.h2: Archbishop Boniface and the Appeal to Charles Martel
paras: Gregory continued his predecessor's support for St. Boniface, sending him the pallium in 732 and making him an archbishop with authority to create new dioceses in Germany. Boniface visited Rome in 737–738, and Gregory sent him back with further authority as papal legate.

Closer to home, the Lombard king Liutprand seized several towns of the Roman duchy in 739. Gregory allied with the Lombard dukes of Spoleto and Benevento, rebuilt parts of the walls of Rome and of Civitavecchia, and sent envoys to the Frankish leader Charles Martel, with gifts including the keys of St. Peter's tomb, asking for protection. Charles, then allied with Liutprand, did not intervene, but the appeal foreshadowed the later alliance between the papacy and the Franks. Gregory died on 28 November 741, the same year as Charles Martel and Leo III.

keyFacts: Reign: 18 March 731 – 28 November 741
Born in Syria; last pope born outside Europe until Francis (2013)
Roman synod of 731 excommunicated destroyers of holy images
Sent the pallium to St. Boniface (732), making him an archbishop
Appealed to Charles Martel against the Lombards (739)

faqs.question: Why is Gregory III significant in papal history?
faqs.answer: He was the last pope to seek an imperial representative's approval of his election, he firmly condemned iconoclasm, and his appeal to Charles Martel was the first step toward the papacy's later alliance with the Franks.

faqs.question: Who was the next pope born outside Europe after Gregory III?
faqs.answer: Pope Francis, born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and elected in 2013, nearly thirteen centuries later.

faqs.question: Did Charles Martel help Gregory III against the Lombards?
faqs.answer: No. Charles received the pope's envoys and gifts but, being allied with the Lombard king Liutprand, did not send help. The Frankish alliance came only under his son Pepin.
